# 🏠 BOB's Ultimate Smart Home Offline Survival Guide
### *Stay in Control When the Storm Knocks Out Your Internet*

---

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The Core Problem**: Most smart home devices rely on cloud servers + internet to function. When your router or ISP goes down, you lose control. The fix is building a **local-first** smart home that works entirely on your LAN (local area network) — no cloud, no internet required.

---

## 🧠 The Master Strategy: Local-Only Control

Think of it in **3 layers**:

```
Layer 1: LOCAL NETWORK (your own hardware - survives router/ISP outage)
Layer 2: LOCAL HUB (brain of your home - runs offline)
Layer 3: LOCAL-CAPABLE DEVICES (smart devices with local APIs)
```

You need hardware and devices that work at **Layer 1 & 2** without ever needing Layer 3 (the internet).

---

## 🔧 STEP 1 — Build a Local Network WITHOUT the ISP Box

When the ISP modem/router goes down, you still need a **local network** so your devices can talk to each other.

### Option A: Dedicated Local Router (Best)
Buy a **second router** that acts as a LOCAL-ONLY access point:

| Hardware | Purpose | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **GL.iNet GL-MT3000** (Beryl AX) | Travel/backup router, runs OpenWrt | ~\$80 |
| **Raspberry Pi 4 + hostapd** | DIY Wi-Fi access point | ~\$60 |
| **TP-Link TL-WR902AC** | Tiny travel router | ~\$30 |
| **Ubiquiti UniFi AP** | Enterprise-grade local AP | ~\$100+ |

**How it works**:
- Connect this router to a **switch** (not the ISP modem)
- All smart devices connect to THIS router's Wi-Fi (not your ISP Wi-Fi)
- The hub/controller (see Step 2) also connects here
- When ISP goes out → local router still broadcasts Wi-Fi → everything still talks

> [!TIP]
> **Set your backup router's SSID and password IDENTICAL to your main router.** Devices will automatically reconnect to it if the main one drops. Use the same IP range (e.g., `192.168.1.x`) so no reconfiguration is needed.

### Option B: Raspberry Pi as Access Point
```bash
# On a Raspberry Pi 4, install:
sudo apt install hostapd dnsmasq
# Configure hostapd for your SSID/password
# Configure dnsmasq for DHCP
# Result: your own Wi-Fi network with no internet needed
```

### Option C: Phone as Hotspot (Emergency Fallback)
Your phone's hotspot creates a Wi-Fi network. If devices are pre-configured to auto-connect and you set the hotspot SSID/password to match your home network name — they may reconnect automatically.

---

## 🧠 STEP 2 — The Local Smart Home Hub (The Brain)

This is the **most critical piece**. A local hub runs on YOUR hardware and controls all devices WITHOUT cloud servers.

### 🥇 Home Assistant (Best Choice — Free & Open Source)
**Runs on a Raspberry Pi, old PC, NUC, or NAS.**

```
https://www.home-assistant.io/
```

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Works offline** | 100% local, no cloud dependency |
| **Supports 3000+ integrations** | Lights, locks, cameras, HVAC, sensors... |
| **Automations run locally** | If internet is down, automations still fire |
| **Mobile app** | Works on local Wi-Fi even with no internet |
| **Voice control** | Works via Wyoming/Whisper locally |

**Hardware to run it:**
- Raspberry Pi 4 (4GB) — ~\$55 + SD card
- Intel NUC mini PC — ~\$150+
- Old laptop/desktop — free if you have one
- **Home Assistant Green** (official device) — ~\$99
- **Home Assistant Yellow** — ~\$130

**Install:**
```bash
# Flash Home Assistant OS to SD card using Balena Etcher
# Boot Pi → go to http://homeassistant.local:8123
# Done — runs 100% locally
```

### Other Local Hub Options

| Hub | Local? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Hubitat Elevation** | ✅ Yes | Paid device (~\$150), rock solid offline |
| **openHAB** | ✅ Yes | Free, Java-based, complex |
| **Node-RED** | ✅ Yes | Flow-based automation, pairs with HA |
| **HomeSeer** | ✅ Yes | Paid, powerful, Windows/Linux |
| **Vera Plus** | ⚠️ Partial | Z-Wave/Zigbee local, some cloud |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Avoid SmartThings, Google Home, Amazon Alexa as your PRIMARY hub** — they require internet to function. They can be secondary voice interfaces only.

---

## 📡 STEP 3 — Use Local-Compatible Protocols (Not Cloud-Dependent)

The RIGHT way to connect smart devices — protocols that work on your local network:

### ✅ Protocols That Work 100% Offline

| Protocol | Range | Speed | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Zigbee** | ~30ft mesh | Fast | Lights, sensors, plugs |
| **Z-Wave** | ~100ft mesh | Fast | Locks, switches, sensors |
| **Thread/Matter** | ~30ft mesh | Very fast | New gen everything |
| **Wi-Fi (local API)** | Full home | Very fast | Bulbs, plugs, cams |
| **Bluetooth (BLE)** | ~30ft | Fast | Locks, sensors |
| **Insteon** | ~150ft | Very fast | Switches, dimmers |
| **KNX** | Building-wide | Very fast | Pro installations |

### ⚠️ Protocols to AVOID for Local-Only Use
- **Pure cloud Wi-Fi devices** (Wiz, some Wyze, older TP-Link) — require internet
- **Proprietary cloud hubs** (Ring, Nest without local API) — cloud-dependent

---

## 💡 STEP 4 — Smart Devices That Work Locally (The Device List)

### 🔦 LIGHTING

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Hub Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Philips Hue** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local API | Hue Bridge + HA |
| **IKEA TRADFRI/Dirigera** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | HA Integration |
| **Lutron Caseta** | Clear Connect RF | ✅ Full local API | Lutron Smart Bridge |
| **Inovelli (Z-Wave)** | Z-Wave | ✅ Full local | Z-Wave stick + HA |
| **Sengled** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | Zigbee coordinator |
| **Shelly (bulbs/dimmers)** | Wi-Fi | ✅ Local API + MQTT | Direct to HA |
| **ESPHome DIY** | Wi-Fi | ✅ 100% local | HA native |
| **Tasmota-flashed devices** | Wi-Fi | ✅ 100% local | MQTT broker |

### 🔒 SMART LOCKS

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Schlage Encode Plus** | Z-Wave + BLE | ✅ Z-Wave local | Needs Z-Wave hub |
| **Yale Assure Z-Wave** | Z-Wave | ✅ Full local | Best offline lock |
| **Kwikset Halo** | Z-Wave | ✅ Full local | Good reliability |
| **August Pro (Z-Wave)** | Z-Wave | ✅ Full local | Retrofit existing |
| **Danalock** | Z-Wave + Zigbee | ✅ Full local | EU popular |
| **August Wi-Fi** | Wi-Fi | ⚠️ Partial local | Some cloud |
| **Wyze Lock** | BLE + Wi-Fi | ❌ Cloud-heavy | Avoid for offline |

> [!WARNING]
> **Smart locks are critical for safety.** Always ensure Z-Wave or Zigbee variants — never rely on a Wi-Fi lock that needs cloud. Also keep **physical backup keys** for true offline emergencies.

### 🌡️ THERMOSTATS

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ecobee** | Wi-Fi | ⚠️ Partial | Has local API but limited |
| **Honeywell T6 Pro Z-Wave** | Z-Wave | ✅ Full local | Best offline thermostat |
| **Radio Thermostat CT100** | Z-Wave | ✅ Full local | Budget option |
| **Stelpro STZB402** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | Electric heat |
| **Nest** | Wi-Fi | ❌ Cloud-only | Avoid |
| **ESPHome DIY Thermostat** | Wi-Fi | ✅ 100% local | Advanced DIY |

### 📷 SECURITY CAMERAS

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Reolink** | Wi-Fi/PoE | ✅ Full local RTSP | Record to NAS locally |
| **Amcrest** | Wi-Fi/PoE | ✅ Full local RTSP | Good local API |
| **Hikvision** | PoE | ✅ Full local | Pro grade |
| **Dahua** | PoE | ✅ Full local | Pro grade |
| **Frigate NVR (software)** | N/A | ✅ 100% local | Runs on HA/Pi, AI detection |
| **Wyze Cam** | Wi-Fi | ❌ Cloud-heavy | Avoid for offline |
| **Ring** | Wi-Fi | ❌ Cloud-only | Avoid |

> [!TIP]
> Run **Frigate** (open source NVR) on a local machine. It processes camera feeds entirely offline, has AI person/car detection, and integrates directly with Home Assistant.

### 🔌 SMART PLUGS & SWITCHES

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Shelly Plug/Shelly 1** | Wi-Fi | ✅ Full local API | Best Wi-Fi plug, MQTT |
| **SONOFF (Tasmota)** | Wi-Fi | ✅ Full local | Flash with Tasmota |
| **Aeotec Z-Wave Plug** | Z-Wave | ✅ Full local | Reliable |
| **Innr Smart Plug** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | Good Zigbee plug |
| **Peanut Plug** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | Budget option |

### 🚪 GARAGE DOORS

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ratgdo (wired)** | Wi-Fi/ESPHome | ✅ 100% local | Best option, ~\$30 |
| **Meross Garage** | Wi-Fi | ⚠️ Partial local | Some cloud needed |
| **Chamberlain/myQ** | Wi-Fi | ❌ Cloud-only | Actively blocks local |
| **Shelly 1 DIY** | Wi-Fi | ✅ 100% local | Wire to door button |

> [!CAUTION]
> **myQ / Chamberlain** actively BLOCKS third-party local access. If your garage door is myQ, replace the controller with a **Ratgdo** board (~\$30) for full local control.

### 💧 WATER / SENSORS

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Aqara Water Sensor** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | Cheap and reliable |
| **SmartThings Multipurpose** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | Door/window/temp |
| **Shelly Flood** | Wi-Fi | ✅ Full local | Water leak detection |
| **Zigbee Motion Sensors (any)** | Zigbee | ✅ Full local | Many options |

### 🎵 AUDIO / MEDIA

| Device | Protocol | Local Support | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Snapcast** | LAN | ✅ 100% local | Multi-room audio |
| **Music Assistant (HA)** | LAN | ✅ 100% local | Local music library |
| **Kodi** | LAN | ✅ 100% local | Local media server |
| **Plex (local)** | LAN | ✅ Local mode | Streams without internet |
| **Sonos** | Wi-Fi | ⚠️ Partial | Local if no cloud updates |

### 🗣️ VOICE CONTROL (Offline)

| Solution | Runs On | Offline? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wyoming + Whisper (HA)** | Pi 4 / PC | ✅ 100% local | Best local voice |
| **Piper TTS (HA)** | Pi 4 / PC | ✅ 100% local | Local text-to-speech |
| **Rhasspy** | Pi / Docker | ✅ 100% local | Standalone voice assistant |
| **Mycroft** | Pi / PC | ✅ 100% local | Open source voice AI |
| **Alexa / Google Home** | Cloud | ❌ Internet req'd | Won't work offline |

---

## ⚡ STEP 5 — Power: Keep Everything Running During an Outage

Your smart home hub and network need power to work even if the lights flicker out.

### UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply)
**Connect these devices to a UPS:**
- Your local router/AP
- Your smart home hub (Pi/NUC)
- Zigbee/Z-Wave coordinator
- Network switch
- NAS/camera storage

| UPS | Runtime | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **APC Back-UPS 600VA** | 1-2 hrs | Router + Pi hub |
| **CyberPower CP1500** | 2-4 hrs | Full rack setup |
| **Eaton 5S 700VA** | 1-3 hrs | Compact setup |

> [!TIP]
> A Raspberry Pi 4 draws only ~5-8 watts. A 600VA UPS can keep it running for **4-6+ hours** during an outage.

### Power Outage — Device Behavior Planning
```
When power returns after a flicker:
- Zigbee/Z-Wave devices: auto-rejoin mesh
- Wi-Fi devices: auto-reconnect if router is on backup power
- Local hub: auto-restart (configure HA to start on boot)
- Automations: fire normally once devices reconnect
```

Set Home Assistant automations:
```yaml
# Auto-notify when power is restored
automation:
  - alias: "Power Restored Alert"
    trigger:
      - platform: homeassistant
        event: start
    action:
      - service: notify.mobile_app
        data:
          message: "Home Assistant restarted - system online"
```

---

## 🗺️ STEP 6 — Full Local Architecture Blueprint

```
                    [ STORM HITS - ISP DOWN ]
                           |
              ┌────────────┴────────────┐
              │                         │
    ┌─────────▼─────────┐    ┌─────────▼─────────┐
    │  LOCAL ROUTER      │    │  UPS BACKUP POWER  │
    │  (No internet)     │    │  (Keeps it alive)  │
    │  192.168.1.x       │    └───────────────────┘
    └─────────┬─────────┘
              │ Local Wi-Fi / LAN
    ┌─────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
    │            HOME ASSISTANT HUB                   │
    │         (Raspberry Pi 4 / NUC)                 │
    │  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────┐ │
    │  │ Zigbee   │  │ Z-Wave   │  │ MQTT Broker  │ │
    │  │ Coord.   │  │ Stick    │  │ (Mosquitto)  │ │
    │  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘  └──────┬───────┘ │
    └───────┼─────────────┼───────────────┼─────────┘
            │             │               │
     ┌──────┴──────┐ ┌────┴────┐ ┌───────┴──────┐
     │ Zigbee Mesh │ │Z-Wave   │ │ Shelly / Wi-Fi│
     │             │ │ Mesh    │ │ Devices       │
     │ • Lights    │ │         │ │               │
     │ • Sensors   │ │ • Locks │ │ • Plugs       │
     │ • Plugs     │ │ • HVAC  │ │ • Switches    │
     │ • Cameras   │ │ • Garage│ │ • Sensors     │
     └─────────────┘ └─────────┘ └───────────────┘
```

---

## 📱 STEP 7 — Access Your Home Locally (No Internet)

When internet is out, access Home Assistant via **local IP or mDNS**:

### On Your Phone (same Wi-Fi as hub):
```
http://homeassistant.local:8123
# OR
http://192.168.1.xxx:8123  (whatever your Pi's IP is)
```

### Set a Static IP on the Hub:
Make sure Home Assistant always gets the **same IP** (e.g., `192.168.1.10`):
- Set a DHCP reservation in your router for the Pi's MAC address
- Or configure a static IP directly on the Pi

### For Remote Access When Internet IS Working (Optional):
- **Nabu Casa** (\$6.50/mo) — official HA cloud relay
- **Tailscale** (free) — VPN that works even when one end has internet
- **WireGuard VPN** (free) — self-hosted VPN on your router

---

## 🚨 STEP 8 — The "Storm Kit" Emergency Checklist

Print this and tape it inside a cabinet:

```
□ Local router on UPS — broadcasting SSID: [YOUR_SSID]
□ Home Assistant Pi on UPS — at 192.168.1.10
□ Phone connected to local Wi-Fi
□ Open browser → http://192.168.1.10:8123
□ Control lights, locks, cameras from HA dashboard
□ Voice control: speak to local Rhasspy/Wyoming device
□ Physical key backup for front door: [LOCATION]
□ Physical flashlights: [LOCATION]
□ Generator for extended outage: [LOCATION]
```

---

## 🛒 The BOB Starter Kit (Budget Build ~\$200-300)

| Item | Cost | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Raspberry Pi 4 (4GB) + case + SD | \$70 | HA Hub |
| ConBee II or Sonoff Zigbee stick | \$30 | Zigbee coordinator |
| Aeotec Z-Stick Gen5+ | \$45 | Z-Wave controller |
| TP-Link TL-WR902AC router | \$30 | Local-only backup AP |
| APC Back-UPS 600VA UPS | \$70 | Backup power |
| **Total** | **~\$245** | **Full offline hub** |

Then replace/add devices over time using the **Zigbee/Z-Wave** options from the list above.

---

## 🎯 Quick Wins You Can Do TODAY

1. **Download the Home Assistant app** on your phone → it has a local fallback mode
2. **Note your router's IP address** (usually `192.168.1.1` or `192.168.0.1`)
3. **Check if any devices you own have a local API** (Shelly, Hue, etc.)
4. **Put your router on a UPS** — this alone solves most "storm" scenarios
5. **Flash SONOFF/cheap plugs with Tasmota** — makes them cloud-free instantly

---

> [!NOTE]
> **The Golden Rule of Offline Smart Homes**: If a device's box says "requires internet connection" or "works with Alexa/Google" as the ONLY control method — it's cloud-dependent. Look for devices that advertise **local API**, **Z-Wave**, **Zigbee**, or **Matter** support.

---

class OccupancyLearner:
    """Learns daily occupancy patterns from motion sensor history."""
    
    def __init__(self, data_file: str = None):
        self.data_file = data_file or str(Path(__file__).parent / "data" / "occupancy.json")
        self.motion_history = {} # room -> list of timestamps

        self._load_data()

    def _load_data(self):
        if Path(self.data_file).exists():
            try:
                with open(self.data_file, 'r') as f:
                    data = json.load(f)
                    self.motion_history = data.get('history', {})
                    self.patterns = data.get('patterns', {})
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Error loading occupancy data: {e}")

    def record_motion(self, room: str, timestamp: float) -> None:
        """Records a motion event in a room."""
        if room not in self.motion_history:
            self.motion_history[room] = []
        self.motion_history[room].append(timestamp)

    def learn_patterns(self) -> dict:
        """Learns hour-by-hour occupancy probability."""
        logger.info("Learning occupancy patterns from history...")
        for room, timestamps in self.motion_history.items():
            # Create a 24-hour histogram
            hour_counts = np.zeros(24)
            total_days = set()
            
            for ts in timestamps:
                dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(ts)
                hour_counts[dt.hour] += 1
                total_days.add(dt.date())
                
            num_days = len(total_days) if len(total_days) > 0 else 1
            # Simple probability: max 1.0
            probabilities = np.clip(hour_counts / (num_days * 5), 0.0, 1.0) # Assuming 5+ events in an hour means highly likely occupied
            self.patterns[room] = probabilities.tolist()
            
        return self.patterns

    def predict_occupied(self, room: str, time_of_day: datetime) -> bool:
        """Predicts if a room is likely occupied at a given time."""
        if room not in self.patterns:
            return False
        
        prob = self.patterns[room][time_of_day.hour]
        return prob > 0.5

    def get_optimal_automation_times(self, room: str) -> list[TimeWindow]:
        """Returns time windows where automation (like heating/cooling) makes sense."""
        if room not in self.patterns:
            return []
            
        windows = []
        probs = self.patterns[room]
        
        in_window = False
        start = 0
        
        for hour in range(24):
            if probs[hour] > 0.3 and not in_window:
                in_window = True
                start = hour
            elif probs[hour] <= 0.3 and in_window:
                in_window = False
                windows.append(TimeWindow(start, hour, float(np.mean(probs[start:hour]))))
                
        if in_window:
            windows.append(TimeWindow(start, 24, float(np.mean(probs[start:24]))))
            
        return windows

        target_path = path or self.data_file

import sys
import os
import argparse
from datetime import datetime
from collections import defaultdict

sys.path.append(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'ai'))
from occupancy_learner import OccupancyLearner

def parse_casas_dataset(file_path: str, ol: OccupancyLearner):
    """
    Parses a standard WSU CASAS Smart Home dataset file.
    Expected format per line:
    YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmmmmm SensorID SensorValue [Activity]
    e.g., 2010-11-04 00:03:50.209589 M003 ON Sleep
    """
    print(f"📂 Loading CASAS Dataset from: {file_path}")
    print("⏳ Processing millions of rows... This may take a moment.")
    
    line_count = 0
    motion_events = 0
    
    try:
        with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            for line in f:
                line_count += 1
                parts = line.strip().split()
                if len(parts) < 4:
                    continue
                
                date_str = parts[0]
                time_str = parts[1]
                sensor_id = parts[2]
                sensor_value = parts[3]
                
                # We only care about Motion sensors (usually start with 'M' in CASAS)
                # and when they are triggered 'ON'
                if sensor_id.startswith('M') and sensor_value == 'ON':
                    try:
                        # Parse the timestamp: 2010-11-04 00:03:50.209589
                        dt_str = f"{date_str} {time_str}"
                        # CASAS sometimes drops the microseconds
                        if '.' in time_str:
                            dt = datetime.strptime(dt_str, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f")
                        else:
                            dt = datetime.strptime(dt_str, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
                        
                        # In a real setup, you'd map 'M003' to 'Living_Room', etc.
                        # For now, we group by the raw sensor ID.
                        ol.record_motion(sensor_id, dt.timestamp())
                        motion_events += 1
                        
                    except ValueError:
                        continue
                        
                if line_count % 500000 == 0:
                    print(f"   -> Parsed {line_count} rows...")
                    
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"❌ ERROR: File not found at {file_path}")
        print("Please download the CASAS Aruba dataset (or similar) from Zenodo and place it here.")
        sys.exit(1)
        
    print(f"✅ Successfully parsed {line_count} total rows.")
    print(f"✅ Extracted {motion_events} valid motion events.")
    
    # Trigger the ML learning phase
    ol.learn_patterns()
    print("🧠 BOB has finished learning the actual human occupancy patterns from the CASAS data.")
    return ol

def print_occupancy_heatmap(ol: OccupancyLearner, room: str):
    """Prints an ASCII heatmap of a room's probability of being occupied by hour."""
    print(f"\n🔥 IRL OCCUPANCY HEATMAP: SENSOR {room} 🔥")
    print("Hour | Probability Bar")
    print("-----|--------------------------------------------------")
    
    for hour in range(24):
        # We query the AI to predict if occupied based on a datetime matching that hour
        dt = datetime(2026, 8, 20, hour, 0)
        is_occupied = ol.predict_occupied(room, dt)
        
        # Display logic
        bar = "█" * 30 if is_occupied else "░" * 5
        status = "HIGH" if is_occupied else "LOW "
        print(f"{hour:02d}:00 | {bar} ({status})")

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Analyze WSU CASAS Dataset with BOB AI.')
    parser.add_argument('dataset_path', type=str, help='Path to the CASAS dataset file (e.g., data.txt)')
    parser.add_argument('--sensor', type=str, default='M003', help='Specific sensor ID to map (default M003)')
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    
    ol = OccupancyLearner()
    parse_casas_dataset(args.dataset_path, ol)
    
    # Print the heatmap for the requested sensor
    print_occupancy_heatmap(ol, args.sensor)

if __name__ == "__main__":

# IBM Bob Utilization Statement

**Project:** BOB Smart Home Offline Survival System
**Hackathon:** IBM TechXchange 2026 Pre-conference Dev Day Hackathon

### How IBM Bob Was Utilized
For this project, **IBM Bob 2.0** was utilized not just as a code assistant, but as a full **Agentic Engineering Team**. By leveraging IBM Bob's multi-agent capabilities, we transformed a high-level conceptual problem (smart homes failing during internet outages) into a production-ready, enterprise-scaled solution. 

Specifically, IBM Bob was utilized to:
1. **Multi-Agent Orchestration:** We deployed IBM Bob to spawn five parallel subagents (`Smart Home Builder`, `Graphite Metrics`, `Watson AI`, `Dashboard UI`, and `Enterprise Architect`). These agents worked concurrently to build different stack layers of the project simultaneously.
2. **Machine Learning Generation:** IBM Bob was used to write and refine the edge-native machine learning models (`scikit-learn` Random Forest for storm prediction and Isolation Forest for anomaly detection).
3. **Infrastructure & DevOps:** IBM Bob generated the Kubernetes (K3s) manifests, Nginx load balancer configurations, and EMQX Docker Compose files to prove the system could scale to an enterprise level.
4. **Data Simulation & Chaos Testing:** To prove the concept without risking real-world hardware, we tasked IBM Bob with generating synthetic human occupancy data and writing a "Chaos Monkey" script to heavily stress-test the local API via multi-threaded HTTP bombardment.
5. **Patent & Prior Art Research:** We utilized IBM Bob's research agent to scrape web data and patent databases, validating that the specific combination of localized AI and predictive load-shedding was a unique, uncrowded intellectual property space.

IBM Bob acted as the ultimate technical co-founder, enabling rapid prototyping, deep architectural scaling, and rigorous closed-loop testing within the hackathon time limits.
